central circular or oval feature on the face/torso

justification: The strongest correspondence is that both present a front-facing anthropomorphic image organized symmetrically on a tall vertical field, with paired eyes and a central circular feature among curving linear motifs. The biggest difference is that A shows a detailed full-bodied standing figure with limbs, headdress, ornaments, and many subsidiary beings or masks, while B is a much more schematic block-like figure or face with few added iconographic elements.
